四级核心词汇 · 05英文原文

A Name at the Top of the Form

表格顶端的那个名字 · 595 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1At a campus clinic, nurse Mara found two forms clipped together. The first named a pupil who had injured his wrist. The second described fever, cough, and acute pain in the throat. The reception queue was long. With the second name absent, a volunteer assumed both pages belonged to one person. Mara stopped the visit before anyone could prescribe a remedy based on the wrong record. She asked the boy to describe what had happened.

2He was conscious but dizzy. A fall had left a wound near his elbow, a swollen thumb, and a cut on his lip. He assured Mara he had not lost consciousness. A doctor examined the joint to see whether the bone was intact. A nurse applied a bandage. The doctor explained that an injury and an infectious illness required different checks. An expert could not diagnose either one from the other person's form.

3Mara dialed the number on the second page. A father said his infant had become ill overnight. A medical assistant had written down a new contact number but had left the name blank. A laboratory could assess a sample for a virus only after staff confirmed whose sample it was. Mara arranged a prompt review. As a precaution, she asked the volunteer to put a name field on every page.

4A supervisor asked why the wrong name had seemed plausible. Both patients had reported fatigue and a headache. One had had excessive heat exposure. The other had breathing problems. A test could show if a patient was deficient in a vitamin or if an organ was under stress. The test would vary by case. Mara made the differences clear. An accurate record gave the physician an adequate basis for choosing a check. A professional diagnosis still depended on which symptom belonged to which person. They could sympathize with an anxious parent and give a proper response.

5The boy was ashamed to mention that he was anxious about a sports trial. A teammate had mocked his visits for therapy. Mara listened to his frustration. Her experience in psychology helped her understand the psychological pressure behind his question. Distress could affect sleep and food intake. She offered to arrange a private conversation with a counselor. A teammate's opinion did not oblige him to ignore pain. He needed guidance on when to resume exercise.

6At a staff meeting, a physician recalled a case of acute alcohol poisoning. Neglect of a small detail could delay treatment and have fatal results. The team drew up a guideline for identifying patients before they administered a drug. The change would involve reception staff as well as doctors. They made room for private questions regarding depression, treatment, or the effects of medicine.

7A volunteer proposed publishing the incidence of record errors. Mara supported the idea, but the report had to protect personal details. A nurse collected anonymous feedback on a voluntary basis. Before long, the team was aware of a second problem. When the printer ran out of paper, it sometimes failed to print the last page. They changed the procedure so that every patient received a complete set of essential instructions.

8The pupil returned a month later. His wrist had undergone a gradual recovery. He was ready to discuss a regular routine with his therapist. He recognized the bold field and informed a father what it was for. The clinic eventually found that the check delayed patients only slightly. Mara kept the old clip in her drawer. It reminded her that two ordinary pieces of paper could tell a misleading story when put together.

四级核心词汇 · 05中文译文

表格顶端的那个名字

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1校园诊所里，护士玛拉发现两张表夹在了一起。第一张写着一名手腕受伤的学生，第二张写着发烧、咳嗽和急剧的喉咙痛。接待处排着长队。第二张没有名字，一名志愿者就以为两页说的是同一个人。玛拉在有人可能照着错误的记录开药之前暂停了问诊，请男孩先说说发生了什么。

2男孩神志清醒，却有些头晕。他摔了一跤，手肘附近有伤，拇指肿了，嘴唇上还有一道口子。他向玛拉保证自己没有失去过意识。医生检查了关节，看骨头是否完好。护士为他缠上绷带。医生解释，外伤和传染性疾病要做的检查不同。再有经验的人也无法用另一个人的表格给眼前的人诊断。

3玛拉拨了第二页的号码。接电话的父亲说，他家婴儿夜里病了。一名医务助理写上了新的联系电话，却把姓名栏空着。实验室能检测样本里有没有病毒，前提是先确认样本是谁的。玛拉及时安排了复查。为免再出错，她请志愿者在每一页都加上姓名栏。

4主管问，为什么会以为第二张也是这个男孩的。两名患者都说自己疲倦、头痛，其中一人长时间待在高温环境里，另一人有呼吸问题。检查有可能发现缺乏某种维生素，也有可能发现某个器官承受着压力，具体查什么，要看个人情况。玛拉把两人的不同之处写清楚。准确的记录能让医生有足够的依据选择检查项目，专业诊断仍要先分清症状是谁的。医护人员可以体谅着急的家长，再作合适的回应。

5男孩不好意思提起，自己正在为一次体育测试发愁。队友曾嘲笑他去接受治疗。玛拉听他说出心里的挫败。她学过心理学，能理解这件事给他带来的压力。忧虑会影响睡眠和进食，她可以安排一次和咨询员单独谈话的机会。队友怎么看，都用不着他硬忍着疼。他需要有人指点，什么时候可以恢复运动。

6在员工会上，一位医生回想起一例急性酒精中毒。漏看一个小细节，就可能耽误治疗，造成致命后果。团队写了一份指引，要求用药前核对患者身份，接待人员和医生都要参与。他们还腾出一个私密的地方，让人可以询问抑郁、治疗或药物作用。

7一位志愿者建议公布病历记录的出错率。玛拉赞同，同时要求保护个人信息。护士让愿意反馈的人匿名写下遇到的问题。团队很快发现了第二处漏洞。打印机一缺纸，有时就漏印最后一页。他们调整了流程，让每位患者都能收到一整套必要说明。

8一个月后，男孩再次来到诊所。他的手腕逐渐恢复，准备和治疗师商量一套固定的训练安排。他认出加粗的姓名栏，也告诉旁边一位父亲那一栏用来做什么。诊所后来发现，多做一次核对，只让患者多等了一小会儿。玛拉把旧夹子留在抽屉里。它提醒她，两张普通的纸夹在一起，就可能让人听到一个完全走样的故事。
